essays.text: 英譯中：請將下面這段英文譯成正確、流暢的中文（30 分）The pervasive integration of smart surveillance in modern residentialcomplexes has sparked a contentious debate over consumer privacy. Whileproperty managers advocate for heightened security, residents often object tothe unconsented gathering of their biometric data. Under basic tort law,individuals possess a "reasonable expectation of privacy" in their domiciles, aright that technology constantly threatens to encroach upon. Users routinelyclick "agree" to lengthy terms of service, but this passive acquiescence doesnot necessarily constitute legally binding consent under scrutinized consumerprotection frameworks. As regulatory bodies struggle to reconciletechnological convenience with constitutional protections, consumers mustremain vigilant, understanding that safeguarding digital privacy is no longermerely a personal preference, but a vital civil liberty.

中譯英：請將下面這段中文譯成正確、流暢的英文（30 分）越來越多企業與政府機構開始利用演算法協助做出重要決策，例如篩選求職者、審核貸款申請以及分配公共資源。支持者認為，演算法可以提高效率並降低人為偏見，但批評者指出，演算法本身也可能受到訓練資料或設計方式的影響，而產生不公平的結果。此外，當民眾因演算法的決定而受到不利影響時，他們是否有權知道決策依據，甚至要求重新審查，也逐漸成為法律與倫理的重要議題。如何兼顧效率、透明度與公平性，仍有待社會持續討論。

英文作文：請根據下面說明寫一篇約 250-300 字的英文作文（40 分）Many decisions are evaluated according to their immediate outcomes.However, some consequences remain hidden because they emerge gradually,affect people indirectly, or become visible only after a long period of time.These "invisible costs" may include reduced public trust, weakened socialrelationships, environmental degradation, or the loss of future opportunities.Although such costs are difficult to measure, they may ultimately outweighthe immediate benefits of a decision.Write a short essay of 250-300 words to (1) discuss why invisible costs areoften overlooked in decision-making, and (2) explain how individuals orpolicymakers can make decisions that better account for long-term andindirect consequences.
